title: Social media as health educator: An assessment of the understandability and accuracy of tiktok content about contraception
screen_reason: This is a QUALITY-instrument study: 174 educational contraception TikTok videos scored on PEMAT-A/V (understandability/actionability) and a modified CRAAP test (currency, relevance, authority, accuracy, purpose), reported as domain mean scores. Under Sec. 1 a quality-only study is an EXCLUDE for prevalence; under Sec. 3 the QUALITY row is KEPT and excluded from prevalence, so I have screened it INCLUDE with a single construct=QUALITY row and no CONTENT row. The one item-level share of anything falsity-adjacent is the CRAAP accuracy item 'Information supported by evidence?' (No: 21/174 = 12.1%), which the Discussion glosses as content that 'contradicted or COULD NOT BE CORROBORATED by published evidence'. Because a wholly true video could be coded 'No' merely for lack of corroboration, this fails the Sec. 3 test for CONTENT (judged for truth/falsity against an external ground truth) and is coded QUALITY with borderline=true. An adjudicator who reads the item as a falsity judgement would flip this row to CONTENT; one who applies Sec. 1 literally would flip the paper to EXCLUDE with no rows.

estimates.country: Not stated for the videos (TikTok content retrieved by English contraception hashtags; the study team and framing are United States)
estimates.date: Videos downloaded December 2021 (the 700 most-viewed contraception videos at the time of download); currency scored from that download date
estimates.measure_type: % of educational contraception TikTok videos coded 'No' on the CRAAP accuracy item 'Information supported by evidence?' (i.e. contradicted or not corroborated by published evidence)
estimates.value_raw: Information supported by evidence? No: 21/174 (12.1%) overall; HCP 1/99 (1.0%); non-HCP 20/75 (26.7%); p < 0.001. Yes: 153/174 (87.9%)
estimates.denominator: 174 TikTok videos coded as educational and still assessable, drawn from the 252 educational videos within the 700 most-viewed contraception videos (hashtags #iud, #nexplanon, #birthcontrolpills, #nuvaring, #birthcontrolpatch, #depo, #birthcontrol, #planb) downloaded in December 2021
estimates.definition: A video coded 'No' by two board-certified gynecologists on the CRAAP accuracy item 'Information supported by evidence?'; the Discussion describes this group as content that 'contradicted or could not be corroborated by published evidence'
estimates.misinfo_def: No formal definition. Framing only: "Recent reports suggest a rise of contraceptive misinformation on social media, often urging users to switch to less effective contraception, particularly non-hormonal methods, such as 'natural cycles'"; and "To gauge the degree of misinformation on TikTok, we performed a secondary analysis of the TikTok content analysis study by Stoddard et al. (2024) to evaluate the understandability, actionability, and scientific accuracy of those most-viewed videos containing contraception educational content"
estimates.page_loc: Table 2 (Domains of Accuracy), p. 5; glossed in the Discussion, p. 3
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Two board-certified gynecologists (DB, NJ) coded every video on the modified CRAAP instrument, with discrepancies adjudicated if Cohen's kappa was below 0.7. (The separate PEMAT-A/V coding was done by two reviewers, JKC and MEH-K, with a third, DB, adjudicating; substantial agreement, Cohen's kappa > 0.7, on all items.) The comparator is 'published evidence'/'published evidence-based guidelines', not a named fact-check source; no reliability statistic is reported for the accuracy item itself.
estimates.moderator_quote: To assess video reliability and accuracy, we used relevant questions from a previously modified version of the Currency, Relevance, Authority, Accuracy, and Purpose (CRAAP) test [15], which has been employed in other studies evaluating the accuracy of online health information [16-18]. ... Two board-certified gynecologists (DB, NJ) coded the videos, with discrepancies adjudicated if Cohen's Kappa was < 0.7.
estimates.notes: The value and denominator are unambiguous in Table 2 (153 + 21 = 174); the uncertainty is entirely about the construct, hence borderline=true. Three things an adjudicator should weigh. (1) 'Not supported by evidence' bundles contradiction with mere non-corroboration, which is why I coded QUALITY rather than CONTENT. (2) The denominator is triply selected: top-700 most-viewed (rank-truncated), then the 36% coded educational (252), then the 174 still assessable after deletions (46), account restrictions (16), unassessable brevity/form (11) and near-duplicates (5) - so 78/252 attrition, and deleted videos may plausibly be the less accurate ones, biasing accuracy upward. (3) HCP vs non-HCP is the paper's headline split (1.0% vs 26.7%), but since the construct is QUALITY and excluded from prevalence anyway, I recorded the overall figure only and put the split in value_raw rather than creating subgroup rows (R4). The Discussion sentence that glosses this category - 'Overall, the majority of videos scored well on domains of accuracy, though 26.7% of non-HCP content contradicted or could not be corroborated by published evidence' - sits in a two-column page region and so could not be used as the contiguous verbatim source_quote; the Table 2 row is quoted instead.

missed_or_uncertain: Not extracted as rows. (a) All CRAAP and PEMAT-A/V summative means - understandability 74.7% (SD 17.4), actionability 37.7% (SD 40.7), currency 2.91/5, relevance 3.64/4, authority 3.46/5, accuracy 4.93/7, purpose 6.49/8 - are scale means on quality instruments, i.e. QUALITY scale_scores with no share of items; per Sec. 3 a Likert/scale mean with no share is not a row. If the review wants one QUALITY scale_score row, the natural candidate is the overall accuracy mean 4.93 (SD 1.93) out of a possible 0-7. (b) Other Table 2 binary items that touch on content trustworthiness but are quality/format judgements, not veracity: 'Information out of date: Yes 8 (4.8%)'; 'Nature of information: Propaganda 6 (3.5%)', Opinion 33 (19.1%), Facts 134 (77.5%); 'Point of view objective and impartial: No 27 (15.9%)'; 'Political, ideological, cultural, religious biases: Yes 6 (3.5%)'; 'Information avoids overgeneralization: No 30 (17.2%)'; 'What kind of evidence supports the claim? None 17 (10.0%)'. Any of these could be argued into a QUALITY row; none is a falsity share. (c) Engagement concentration: 'Of all views, 79.2% were of HCP-created videos and 20.8% were of non-HCP videos'; 9.8% of videos had over 5 million views, and 15/17 (88.2%) of those were HCP-created. These are concentration of ATTENTION BY CREATOR TYPE, not concentration of misinformation exposure or sharing, so they do not satisfy the CONCENTRATION definition (a top group accounting for a share of MISINFORMATION exposure/sharing) and are not extracted. (d) '36% of the 700 most viewed contraception TikTok videos were educational' (252/700) - a genre share carried over from the authors' prior study (Stoddard et al. 2024), not a veracity share, and cited from another paper (R8).

rob.design: Secondary cross-sectional content analysis. Source cohort: the 700 most-viewed contraception TikTok videos at download in December 2021, retrieved via a published hashtag list for six methods (#iud, #nexplanon, #birthcontrolpills, #nuvaring, #birthcontrolpatch, #depo) plus #birthcontrol and #planb. 252 (36%) had been coded educational ('containing at least one take-home point or fact the creator is educating the viewer on'); of these, 174 were assessable here, 78 lost to account deletion (46), account restriction (16), brevity/form precluding assessment (11) and near-duplicates (5). HCPs (physicians, PAs, midwives, nurses) created 57% (n = 99); non-HCPs 75. Instruments: PEMAT-A/V, 14 validated items, binary yes(1)/no(0), summed and expressed as a percentage of possible points, threshold 70% for 'understandable'/'actionable'; two independent reviewers (JKC, MEH-K) with a third (DB) adjudicating, Cohen's kappa > 0.7 for all items. Modified CRAAP test scored across currency (0-5), relevance (0-4), authority (0-5), accuracy (0-7) and purpose (0-8), coded by two board-certified gynecologists (DB, NJ) with adjudication where kappa < 0.7. Chi-square for item frequencies, t-tests for means, Wilcoxon rank sum for medians, Stata 16.0. Not a sample of users, so no response rate. Declined for review by the Mass General Brigham IRB as non-human research. Some items were scored 'not applicable' for some videos, so per-item denominators vary (e.g. only 4 videos scored on 'breaks information into short sections').
